subject: ADR-231: if_stamp guards either document (protocol 1.11) -- a report stamp guards the figures, the report's stamp ignores the screen chrome, and the ninth blind trial measures both halves
body: A tally pressed again moves every figure and no control, so a snapshot-stamped guard let the second press through. Now if_stamp takes a report stamp and guards the report: the door asks the target for its report stamp now (Plugin.stamp), refuses stale naming the report and read-report since as the way to see which figures changed; a target with no report and a string that is not a stamp of either series are refused invalid_argument by name; the manifest says which document each kind guards; the MCP trace records the guard a call carried. The ninth blind trial -- cell bench, cp bench, deployment log, farm scout, one attempt each, 71 of 107 outcomes and 184 of 275 claims in 602 calls -- ran in two halves: on the door as first built 10 of 11 report-guard refusals were the screen chrome's clock, so the report now names its chrome and the stamp and diff treat it and the open pane as noise; on the fixed door 0 of 131 were, 99 were figures that had moved and 88 of those with the snapshot stamp unmoved. verify_contract 241 to 261, verify_report 252 to 276, verify_mcp 98 to 101, verify_tasks 446 to 466, mutate_contract 116 to 126, mutate_report 153 to 162. docs/OPERATOR.md is the canonical operator manual with the two faults the trial found in it fixed.
